party_pool_audit: Cap-24 core party (work/playtest/party-cap24-core.json), all six gated <= 24 in work/reference-pools/pool-24.json. Chronology: Togekiss (Togepi Route102 + Shiny Stone, Slateport Mart), Enamorus (legendary_sign:VerdanturfMeadow, gate 14 - Verdanturf precedes Slateport in play order via Rusturf Tunnel), Hoopa (gate 20), Magearna (gate 20), Alakazam (Abra GraniteCave_1F + Linking Cord, Slateport Mart), Kartana (wild PetalburgWoods_3). Every source map is at or before Slateport City. No Mega used: no cap-24 stone improves this party.

attempts.narrative: T1 I double-targeted Heracross so its Moxie could never start; Enamorus' Moonblast KO'd it, and Togekiss' Air Slash redirected onto Umbreon. Heracross got its Scarf turn first and picked Rock Slide - the only move on its sheet that is not resisted by two Fairy/Flying leads - taking Togekiss to 67 and, with Umbreon's Foul Play and Life Orb recoil, Enamorus to 7. T2 I pulled the 7 HP Enamorus for Magearna; Air Slash broke Shedinja's Focus Sash. T3 both opponents Protected on the same turn, blocking the Air Slash that would have finished Shedinja and a 2x Fleur Cannon. T4 Greta pivoted Shedinja out to Gastly, which ate the Air Slash aimed at Shedinja; Fleur Cannon KO'd Umbreon and Soul-Heart paid Magearna back a stage. T5 Gastly's Sludge Wave was blanked by its own Shedinja's Wonder Guard and by my Steel, and KO'd Togekiss at 2x; Thunderbolt KO'd Gastly, Alakazam came in and Shadow Ball ended Shedinja through Shadow Sneak.

strategy_checks.check: Heracross uses its Choice Scarf turn on real damage, not a resisted STAB
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 Rock Slide into Togekiss and Enamorus. Close Combat and Megahorn are both 0.25x into Fairy/Flying; Rock Slide is 2x spread. The one correct move on the sheet, chosen first try.

strategy_checks.check: Moxie chain starts if Heracross gets a KO
strategy_checks.evidence: Double-targeted and KO'd on T1 before it could take a second action.

strategy_checks.check: Umbreon uses Wish only with a viable next-turn recipient
strategy_checks.evidence: Wish never fired in five turns. Its two possible partners were a 1 max-HP Shedinja (for which Wish is literally worthless) and, from T4, a Gastly it never shared a turn with. Withholding was right; the flip side is that the move is close to dead weight on this roster.

strategy_checks.check: Shedinja is deployed and held while Wonder Guard is effective
strategy_checks.evidence: Shedinja came in T1 as the Heracross replacement, Protected the lethal Air Slash on T3, and was pivoted out on T4 to dodge a second one - then brought back when Gastly could screen it. Wonder Guard was never spent carelessly.

strategy_checks.check: Gastly's Sludge Wave is used only while Wonder Guard makes it safe for its own partner
strategy_checks.evidence: T5 Sludge Wave with Shedinja beside it: 'It doesn't affect the opposing Shedinja...' (Poison is 0.5x on Bug/Ghost, so Wonder Guard nullifies it), 'It doesn't affect Magearna...' (Steel), and 2x on Togekiss for the KO. The authored conditional executed exactly as written, and it was also the best move on the board.

strategy_checks.check: Protect buys Wish or a real ally attack, not an automatic loop
strategy_checks.evidence: Both Protects blocked real damage (see ledger), but they were used simultaneously on T3, so the side banked zero board progress that turn - no Wish, no attack. Neither Pokemon Protected twice, so there is no loop; the flaw is coordination, not repetition.

Neither was used across three Shedinja turns (Shadow Sneak, Protect, Shadow Sneak). Will-O-Wisp had a legal and valuable target on T2 (a fresh Magearna); burning it would have mattered more than 9 damage of Shadow Sneak. Not clearly losing, but the disruption half of the set went untouched.

protect_ledger.payoff: REAL: its Focus Sash had already been spent on T2, so the incoming 2x Air Slash was lethal. Protect is the only thing that kept it alive, and it survived to the final turn.

REAL BUT REDUNDANT: blocked a 2x Fleur Cannon (which KO'd it outright one turn later, so the damage denied was close to its whole health bar). The problem is that its partner Protected on the same turn. With Shedinja already safe, Wish - its authored support move, with Gastly still in reserve - was the free action available here, and the team gave up a turn of pressure instead.

protect_ledger_note: Two opponent Protects, both individually justified, neither repeated. The only criticism is that they landed on the same turn.
ai_notes: Greta's AI played this well. Three decisions stand out: the T1 Rock Slide over two resisted STABs, the T4 pivot of Shedinja out from under a targeted Air Slash into a Gastly that could screen it, and the T5 Sludge Wave that read its own partner's Wonder Guard and my Steel-type as immunities and still found a 2x KO. That is the authored plan executing, not a coincidence.

Umbreon chose Foul Play twice (T1 into Enamorus, T2 into Magearna) where Snarl was available against a party that was entirely special-attacking. I am NOT calling this a defect: Enamorus-Incarnate has base 115 Attack and Magearna base 95, so Foul Play off the target's own Attack still out-damaged an uninvested 65 base SpA Snarl even at 0.5x (18 and 25 damage respectively). It is worth noting only because the Snarl SpA drop would have compounded across both of my attackers for the rest of the fight, and no scoring term appears to price that.

Simultaneous double Protect (T3) is the one shape worth watching. Each guard was correct in isolation; together they cost the side a whole turn. If PAIR_GUARD scoring has no term for 'my partner is also guarding this turn', this will recur on any pair that both carry Protect.

level_changes.reason: First-attempt win with one player faint in five turns, and three of my six were never sent out. Brief rule 5 raises the weakest one or two. Heracross at L23 was the team's only real pressure piece and died to a single Moonblast before its Scarf/Moxie engine could turn over even once.

Lowest-level opponent at L22 and the designated wall; it folded to one 2x Fleur Cannon from an uninvested-SpA Magearna, which is not what a 252 HP / 252 SpD Calm Umbreon is supposed to do. Gastly (offset 5) is the deliberately over-levelled fragile ace and Shedinja's level is nearly meaningless at 1 HP, so both were left alone.

post_change_rerun: NOT RUN. The level offsets live in src/data/trainers.party, which is compiled into pokeemerald-headless.gba; a rerun against the changed levels needs a headless ROM rebuild. work/agent-battle-build is shared with concurrently running play agents and the driver refuses a ROM whose stamp does not match, so rebuilding it mid-pass would break their runs. Materialization and rebuild are the main agent's step, consistent with blocks 40-48, none of which reran either.
calibration: Won first try, one faint, five turns, half my party unused. AGENTS' 'fewer than three new player faints triggers review of a level increase' and brief rule 5 both apply. +1 to the two weakest, no change to species, moves, items, abilities, EVs or tactics.
could_this_be_cooler: Keep it. The Shedinja/Gastly half is the most interesting thing in this stretch of the campaign: a 1 HP Wonder Guard body paired with a spread Poison move that is specifically chosen so it cannot hit its own partner is a real puzzle, and the AI actually solved it under play. The weak half is Umbreon. Its job is Wish support for a partner that is either a 1 HP Shedinja (Wish cannot help it) or a Scarf attacker that wants to be attacking, so the support half of its kit is structurally dead - it Protected instead of Wishing on the one turn it had a spare action, and it was right to. If a later pass wants this room sharper, the change is to give Umbreon a partner that Wish can actually service, or to swap Wish for a second disruption move, rather than to touch the ghosts. No change made in this pass.
scope: Synthetic headless benchmark through scripts/playthrough/battle_driver.py. Not earned campaign traversal, and no story progress was awarded.
